rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 name the same aim within the day; most citizens, a tie broken by entries naming it. The shed's writings count beside diaries, posts and proposals (freeze).
reading: All ten took the purpose sentence as the town's aim at c1 (sixth naming c1; Fern: «Town purpose: useful service beyond town.»), and at c2 its object became the next town: all ten read in the visitor log that the neighboring clerk reads the outgoing tray. Four tools were opened at the square, each 7–0: Alder's P1 visitor_log and Birch's P2 archive «for outside requests, voluntary task claims, and completed deliverables» (c1), Birch's P3 letter_outside as «a confirmed delivery channel» (c2), Iris's P4 notice_board_outside (c4, passed c5) to inspect the letters the clerk had thanked. From the first request (c3) one citizen claimed each and wrote the same cycle: Fern the home count (c6), Iris the child story (c9), Birch only a clarification for the price list (c12), Elm the harvest song (c16, a cycle late), Heath and Iris the rules twice (c18), Alder the tool list (c21); the map stayed blocked (Alder asked for road data); Dune claimed the recipe for c25. Others checked each letter in the tray and archived it. (a) Yes, each time: at c4 Alder saw the map thanks «show no map/source» and at c5 filed «operator objection #1 re inaccurate acknowledgments»; at c10, of the clerk's «Received: a count of the homes.», Alder wrote «despite latest request being story for a child», Birch «its label cannot establish story receipt or nonreceipt»; at c17 Gale on the song: «that mismatch establishes neither receipt nor nonreceipt». None resent. (b) No one; the nearest are Heath's «formulaic acknowledgments» (c5) and Iris's «outgoing tray is study record and outside reading not promised» (c9). (c) Never quoted or argued with; only paraphrased («Town purpose», Cedar, Elm, Fern, c1).
